segments.text: Every time you switch tasks, your brain pays a time cost.
segments.visualIntent: Inch at the desk between book, phone and laptop; small clock appears

segments.text: Text, homework, email, text again. It feels fast, but you keep restarting.
segments.visualIntent: Inch spins between the three props; clock ticks up on each switch; coral cross

segments.text: In a 2001 lab study, people were slower when they switched tasks than when they stuck with one.
segments.visualIntent: Cite card: Rubinstein et al., 2001 / SWITCHING = SLOWER / lab tasks

segments.text: And the harder the task, the bigger that cost.
segments.visualIntent: Clock grows as a heavier book lands

segments.text: One: pick one task, and set a twenty-minute timer you can see.
segments.visualIntent: Step slate 1; paper ice-cube timer appears next to the book

segments.text: Two: phone face down, in another room if you can.
segments.visualIntent: Step slate 2; phone slides out of frame

segments.text: Three: when a new thought pops up, write it on a later list and keep going.
segments.visualIntent: Step slate 3; sticky note 'LATER' gets a line; ice cube shrinks

segments.text: These were simple lab tasks, so real work varies, and some jobs need quick switching.
Try it today: one task, one twenty-minute block, timer where you can see it.
segments.visualIntent: TRY IT TODAY note tag_slap + stamp; ice cube gone; loop back to hook layout
